== Biography ==
James’s inherited dates are 16 May 1788 and 28 October 1849. The published family-record heading instead gives 1778, while the estate abstract reports 1848. These conflicting years remain unresolved; the earlier dates are retained as attributed information. 
== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-804]] is assessed at 39% (possible). James Thomas’s 16 May 1788 birth is chronologically possible for James born c 1735, although the fifty-three-year paternal generation is relatively long. The inherited family attachment supplies a specific lead.

Possible only; the held adult census and vital citations do not name the father, and the long generation needs testing.

Next useful test: Check the original family birth record or James senior’s probate.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-803 WikiTree profile export for Glasgow-803]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


=== Abbeville family records — 4 November 2026 ===

The register and estate abstract identify [[Glasgow-802|Jane Elizabeth Burdette]] (96%), [[Glasgow-818|Mary Ann McClellan]] (96%) and [[Glasgow-2161|Nancy Clementine Hunter]] (95%) as James’s daughters. Mary and Nancy are new daughter connections. The register gives James and [[Morrow-3682|Margaret Morrow]]’s marriage on 27 February 1810. James’s own [[Glasgow-804|James Glasgow]] father remains only 39% possible; the new daughter evidence does not prove his earlier ancestry.<ref name="GlasgowFamilyBible">Nancy McClellan Feroe, [http://www.tngenweb.org/rutherford/glascow.html The Bible Record of James Glasgow] (2005), transcription from a photocopy sent by Oscar “Pet” Hunter on 20 February 1979. James Glasgow/Margaret Morer (Morrow) marriage, 27 February 1810; Maria Ann, Jane El. and Nancy C. births and McClellan, Burditt and Hunter marriages. The deaths are expressly separately copied family notes, not Bible entries. Original and photocopy uninspected.</ref><ref name="GlasgowEstate1847">[https://genealogytrails.com/scar/pickens/wills_1.htm Wills and Estates Notices], James Glasgow section: Abbeville will dated 12 February 1847 and equity proceedings, October–November 1851, naming Mary McClelan, Jane Burdit and Nancy Hunter among six children. The page attributes the estate material to G. Anne Sheriff, The Carolina Herald and Newsletter, Summer 2005, pp.31–39, Pauline Young Collection. Published abstracts inspected; originals uninspected. Its 1848 death conflicts with the separately copied 1849 family note.</ref><ref name="GlasgowLetter1848">[https://www.argenweb.net/bradley/bios/johnpatton/aqwg01.htm Descendants of John Patton McClellan], published Mary Anne Glasgow McClellan letter to sister Nancy Clementine Glasgow Hunter, 17 September 1848; copy attributed to Hal Glasgow, original reportedly held by Pet Hunter on 20 December 1965. The letter body refers to an unnamed father and deceased mother; explicit parent names are supplied by the accompanying genealogy. Original uninspected; the Hunter-family provenance may overlap the Bible copy.</ref>

Published transcriptions/abstracts inspected, not the Bible, its 1979 photocopy, the will/equity manuscripts or the letter original. The Bible and letter travel through the Hunter family and their online genealogies may be dependent; they are not three independent primary witnesses. James’s inherited 1788 birth conflicts with the Bible page heading’s 1778, and the estate abstract’s 1848 death conflicts with separately copied 1849 death notes. These vital questions and his own [[Glasgow-804|James Glasgow]] father remain separate. No census row, birth year, death year, Scottish ancestry or Thomas M Glasgow identity is reassigned.

The profile dates for James are not corrected from the conflicting years alone. [[Glasgow-3766|Thomas M Glasgow]] remains an unselected comparison: the Bible’s James M/N and the letter’s “Tom” are not automatically his identity. The original estate file and Bible photocopy are the next checks.
